plan_a_advantages: Includes a long run to build endurance, which is vital for trail running.
Incorporates threshold and tempo runs to improve speed and running economy.
Offers a more varied training stimulus, promoting more well-rounded development.
Higher total training volume (225 minutes vs 176 minutes) allows for more adaptation.
plan_b_advantages: Focuses heavily on easy running, which can be beneficial for injury prevention and recovery.
Simplicity of the plan may be easier to adhere to for some athletes.
reasoning: Plan A is the better choice for a trail runner aiming to become faster. While both plans incorporate rest days, Plan A includes a variety of training intensities – easy runs, a long run, aerobic work, and a tempo session – which is crucial for developing speed and endurance. Plan B consists solely of easy runs, which, while beneficial for recovery and building a base, won't sufficiently challenge the athlete to improve their speed. The inclusion of threshold and tempo work in Plan A is essential for increasing lactate threshold and improving running economy, both key factors in trail running performance.
